prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a metal grid enclosure on a concrete ledge to the left and in front (0.3 to 2.5 metres away), a raised rough concrete pillar on the lower-left in frames 3 and 4 (0.3 to 0.6 metres away), the camera wearer's hand holding a wire brush at the bottom (0.3 to 0.5 metres away, within arm's reach of the cage bars), and a second person standing outside the right edge of the cage about 1.5 to 2.5 metres from the wearer and 0.2 metres from the mesh. In frames 1, 2, and 5, this second person's upper body and head are cropped out of the top-right edge of the frame while their torso and legs face left toward the cage (within arm's reach of the right mesh wall); across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns and pitches the camera leftward and downward toward the concrete pillar and lower grid in frames 3 and 4 (moving the standing person out of view) before panning right and upward in frame 5. The map clearly separates the bright foreground metal bars, concrete block, and brush from the mid-ground ground plane in a way that is harder to parse against the dappled sunlight and shadows on the dirt and concrete in RGB alone. However, the depth map is unreliable through the cage openings, where the concrete base and sunlit dirt behind the mesh are rendered nearly pitch black as if infinitely far, and in frame 5 where a third person standing behind the far side of the cage (~3 to 4 metres away) is completely lost behind the bright grid bars.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only two 'person' regions in frames 1 and 2—the camera wearer's lower-left forearm/hand (0.3 to 0.5 metres away) and the standing person on the upper-right (1.5 to 2.0 metres away, about 1.2 metres ahead of the wearer's hand)—plus a single 'person' mask for the wearer's two hands at the bottom of frame 4 (0.3 metres away). In frames 1 and 2, the standing person's mask captures their side-facing torso, wrap, and legs (with their head and shoulders out of view above the frame) next to the cage, while the wearer's hand is below and to the left within arm's reach of the lower cage corner. Across the 5 frames, as the viewpoint turns left and down in frames 3 and 4 and then back right in frame 5, the standing person's mask disappears after frame 2 and the wearer's hand mask drops out in frames 3 and 5. While the map cleanly isolates the human figures from the cluttered background of shadows, bricks, and dirt in frames 1, 2, and 4, it is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the wire brush, the metal cage, and the concrete block, fails to detect the wearer's hand in frames 3 and 5, and completely misses both the right-side person and the distant background person occluded by the cage in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand at the bottom-left of frames 1 and 2 (roughly 0.3 to 0.5 metres from the camera), showing the thumb on the left and fingers curled around the wire brush handle within arm's reach of the metal cage. No yellow body skeletons or additional hand skeletons are rendered anywhere in the scene, even though the RGB strip shows another person standing 1.5 to 2.5 metres away on the right in frames 1, 2, and 5 (facing left toward the cage with their head cropped out of view and hands near the bars) and a distant person behind the cage in frame 5. Across the 5 frames, the wearer's hand skeleton stays in a similar gripping posture in frames 1 and 2 before disappearing completely in frames 3, 4, and 5 as the camera turns left toward the concrete block and then back to the right. The magenta skeleton makes the exact finger articulation and grip orientation on the brush handle easier to see in frames 1 and 2 than in the shadowed RGB image, but the map is unreliable because it misses the wearer's hands in frames 3 through 5 and fails to detect the partially out-of-view or mesh-occluded bodies and hands of the other people across all frames.
